text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:
DIE WELT
- Opposition Social Democrats say there is no chance of a tax reform before general elections due next September
- A second regional court rules against a reform of Germany's notoriously tricky spelling rules.
- A growing row over whether Germany should retain its military draft is expected to put further strains on the coalition government.
- Germany is pumping more money into a campaign to convince ordinary citizens of the need for Europe's currency union.
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Schools in Lower Saxony told not to teach newly-reformed spelling rules.
- Social Democrats (SPD) chief Oskar Lafontaine explains position on tax reform to own party, denying government accusations that he is employing "blocking tactics" as a political strategy.
- German Chamber of Industry and Commerce says government backing for innovation and for small companies is insufficient.
HANDELSBLATT
- Utililty group Veba delights investors with half-year earnings.
- A second attempt to rescue Germany's planned tax reform looks set to fail as government and opposition viewpoints continue to differ.
- German chemical firms benefit from strong export business.
- Financial market traders are still unclear how the arrival of the euro will affect their business.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Defence Minister Volker Ruehe criticises coalition partners the FDP for holding a members poll on whether to retain the army draft.
- Flood risk continues to subside in the east German Oder region.
- Opposition SPD says not willing to compromise on tax reform.
- German court saves British-born cows from slaughter, overriding BSE fears.
- Senior liberal politician Otto Graf Lammbsdorff wants to reduce the power of the Bundesrat upper house of German parliament.
